facts.text: I have pain in my thigh.
It's in the upper part of my right thigh.
It has been getting worse over the past 8 years.
Being active and taking cold baths ease it somewhat.
It got worse after I was hit by a car six months ago.
I take NSAID painkillers every day for the pain.
I take paracetamol every day for the pain.
I also need weak opioid painkillers every day.
My legs are not the same length.
I wear shoe inserts for it.
I'm on sick leave because of the pain.
I don't have any other medical conditions.
My periods started when I was 13.
No one in my family has bone disease.
When I was 11 I had pain in my hip joint; it went away.
At that time they drew fluid from my hip joint with a needle under ultrasound, and the fluid showed no infection.
Six months ago I was hit by a car at the level of my knee; no fracture was found.

findings.name: right thigh examination
findings.result: No skin lesions, café au lait spots, erythema, heat or swelling over the right thigh.

findings.name: leg length measurement
findings.result: Slightly unequal but within normal limits.

findings.name: MRI of the right thigh
findings.result: Significantly increased cortical thickness of the right femoral diaphysis, with partial medullary obliteration and an uneven sclerotic surface.

findings.name: PET-CT
findings.result: Significantly increased cortical thickness of the right femoral diaphysis, with partial medullary obliteration and an uneven sclerotic surface.

findings.name: Tc-99m bone scan
findings.result: Increased uptake in most of the right femoral shaft.

findings.name: genetic testing in blood
findings.result: GNAS1 R201 mutation negative; SQSTM1 mutations negative.

findings.name: bone biopsy of the femoral lesion
findings.result: Thickened bone trabeculae with preserved lamellar structure and accentuated cement lines; no fibrosis, inflammation, alcian positivity, malignancy or neoplasia.

gold.reasoning: 1. Paget’s disease of bone was considered but was unlikely because of the patient’s young age, normal alkaline phosphatase, and metaphyseal sparing — “The young age of our patient, normal alkaline phosphatase, and sparing of the metaphysis of the affected bone made Paget’s disease of bone highly unlikely.” 2. Chronic non-infectious osteomyelitis was ruled out because, despite long-bone predilection, the radiological appearance and histology did not support it — “The long bones are a common location for chronic non-infectious osteomyelitis and this can present in childhood; however, the radiological appearance and bone histology did not provide support for this differential diagnosis.”

notes: Index visit: the referral for 8 years of constant right proximal thigh pain (s001-s012); the hip pain at age 11 and the car accident six months earlier are history.
